newsitem.title: ARMENIA: Armenian police clash with protesters.
newsitem.headline: Armenian police clash with protesters.

text.p: Thousands of Armenians contesting President Levon Ter-Petrosyan's election victory stormed the parliament grounds in the capital Yerevan on Wednesday and riot police fired shots over their heads.

Violence spilled over on the third day of a protest by tens of thousands of demonstrators who say Sunday's election in the Caucasian republic was rigged and that the real winner was former prime minister Vazgen Manukyan.
Some protesters broke through the perimeter fence of parliament after an opposition spokesman shouted through a loudhailer that Manukyan had been arrested -- a report which turned out to be false.
Riot police fired from inside the building. Police who had stood waiting outside while the crowd chanted slogans, then marched towards the demostrators, firing shots over their heads.
People started running or fell to the ground and ambulances began arriving at the parliament building, which was lit up with tracer fire.
No one appeared to have been seriously injured although some protesters said they had been beaten.

Ter-Petrosyan has led Armenia through five years of hardship, caused largely by confrontation with neighbouring Azerbaijan. Conditions have eased in recent months but Armenia has suffered many winters of power cuts and shortages.
A crowd of several thousand remained in a standoff late into the evening with riot police on the street outside the U.S. embassy, about 500 metres (550 yards) from parliament.
Shots continued to echo through the area.
Manukyan had told the demonstrators he was going to parliament to negotiate with the electoral commission and that they should follow him "if I do not come out in half an hour".
Presidential spokesman Shahen Karamanukyan accused Manukyan's movement of trying to stage a coup.
"It was an attempt at a fascist coup which was ordered by one of the leaders of the National Democratic Union (NDU)," he said, denying that Manukyan had been arrested.

Eyewitnesses said that the people who drove the remaining crowd down the street outside the parliament were in plain clothes and armed with various weapons, including packets of explosives designed for crowd control.
"We have won this victory with our blood and we are not going to give it up," they shouted as they advanced on the demonstrators, pushing them away from the presidency.

The election commission said on Wednesday preliminary final results showed Ter-Petrosyan, who has led Armenia since it won independence from the Soviet Union in 1991, with 52.09 percent of votes cast to 41.07 percent for Manukyan.

The electoral commission met earlier on Wednesday to discuss the allegations of irregularities. Commission chairman Khachik Bezirjyan faced angry questions from many of the 20 members of the commission, several of whom are Manukyan supporters.

The NDU, which monitored the count, says it has evidence collected from nearly all the 1,742 polling stations showing Manukyan won the election by 55 to 37 percent, but that regional electoral commissions falsifed the figures.
One NDU leader warned on Wednesday that the protesters might resort to violence and said the situation was "explosive".

"If the president, who directed the falsification of the election, insists on his fraudulent victory, then people will begin to choose dangerous methods. I am afraid this is unavoidable," said NDU parliamentarian Arshat Sadoyan.

The Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE), which has been coordinating 89 international observers, has issued a carefully-worded preliminary report criticising "very serious" irregularities in voting procedures.
It did not question the overall legitimacy of the elections but said its findings did not deal with the counting procedure.
